hunks.baseline: It was a famous family that appeared at least once in every modern wuxia novel.
hunks.sol: It was a famous family bound to appear at least once in every modern wuxia novel.

hunks.baseline: They were supposedly one of Murim’s great families, yet martial arts seemed more like their minor than their major.
hunks.sol: They were supposedly one of Murim’s great families, yet martial arts always seemed more like their minor than their major.

hunks.baseline: They were a family of wise men skilled in broad scholarship, strategy, and mechanisms and formations.
hunks.sol: They were a family of wise men versed in a broad range of scholarship, strategy, and mechanisms and formations.

hunks.sol: As a result, the world called them the Divine Mechanism Zhuge, and in Murim, they handled practically every job that required brains.

hunks.sol: If the strategist of the Murim Alliance in a novel you were reading didn’t have a name that began with Zhuge, it almost felt wrong.

hunks.baseline: Perhaps it was because that image of the Zhuge Clan had been so firmly lodged in my mind that I felt strange seeing these martial artists stride toward us without hesitation.
hunks.sol: Perhaps that image of the Zhuge Clan had been lodged so firmly in my mind that seeing these martial artists stride toward us without hesitation felt strangely unfamiliar.

hunks.baseline: But unfamiliarity wasn’t the only emotion I felt.
hunks.sol: But unfamiliarity wasn’t the only thing I felt.

hunks.sol: The Zhuge Clan’s martial artists lined up on either side of the road like iron towers. A lone figure slowly walked between them.

hunks.baseline: The slender young man wearing robes so white they were almost blinding opened his mouth.
hunks.sol: The slender young man wore robes so white they were almost blinding.

hunks.sol: “The stars shone unusually bright last night. It seems they were heralding the arrival of honored guests. I am the Zhuge Clan’s Lesser Family Head…”

hunks.baseline: I raised my hand high and shouted in delight.
hunks.sol: Delighted, I thrust a hand into the air and shouted.

hunks.baseline: “Not ‘Galgyun’… I’m Zhuge Gyun.”
hunks.sol: “Not ‘Galgyun’… My name is Zhuge Gyun.”

hunks.sol: The Zhuge Clan’s martial artists, who still had no idea who I was, stared at me as if I were some kind of madman. Jeok Cheongang looked at me with a hint of confusion.

hunks.sol: “Yes. I met him at the Star-Array Grand Banquet. But this is the first I’ve heard that he’s the Zhuge Clan’s Lesser Family Head.”

hunks.sol: Before I could say anything else, he turned toward Jeok Cheongang and offered his greetings.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang looked Zhuge Gyun up and down before tossing out a question.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang looked Zhuge Gyun up and down, then tossed out a question.

hunks.sol: “I mean the Fan-Wisdom King, Zhuge Gonghu. The bastard who served as the Murim Alliance’s chief strategist during the Great Faction War.”

hunks.baseline: I had heard both the title and name of the Fan-Wisdom King Zhuge Gonghu.
hunks.sol: I had heard both the title and the name of the Fan-Wisdom King Zhuge Gonghu.

hunks.baseline: He had served as the mind of the Murim Alliance during the Great Faction War and was the foremost contributor to turning the grim tide of the war.
hunks.sol: He had served as the mind of the Murim Alliance during the Great Faction War and had been the foremost contributor to turning around the grim course of the war.

hunks.baseline: That was one reason he had been praised as one of the Ten Kings alongside the other Supreme Peak masters.
hunks.sol: That was one reason he had been hailed as one of the Ten Kings alongside the other Supreme Peak masters.

hunks.baseline: *What a way to refer to someone like that.*
hunks.sol: *And he calls a man like that a bastard.*

hunks.baseline: I had gotten used to seeing Jeok Cheongang act this way, but to everyone else, it must have been a whole new world.
hunks.sol: I had seen Jeok Cheongang act this way so many times that I was used to it, but to everyone else, it must have been a whole new world.

hunks.sol: “H-he was my great-grandfather.”

hunks.sol: “Is that so? No wonder you look a little like him. You look like you’ve got a decent head on your shoulders. Like you’ve got no manners, either.”

hunks.baseline: Since Jeok Cheongang was a man from two generations ago who had lived well past a hundred, even the elders of most prestigious clans and sects couldn’t dare object when he called them, “Hey,” “you,” or “bastard.”

hunks.sol: While I tried to restrain Jeok Cheongang, who had suddenly flown off the handle, Jin Wikyung hurriedly continued.

hunks.baseline: As we moved, I felt countless wary gazes and heard people whispering as they watched us.
hunks.sol: As we moved, I felt countless wary gazes following us and heard the whispers all around.

hunks.sol: I didn’t have long to wonder. The moment we climbed into the carriage, Mungyeong quietly spoke.

hunks.baseline: “It seems we are one person short.”
hunks.sol: “It seems we’re one person short.”

hunks.baseline: “Here, Benefactor!”
hunks.sol: “Over here, Benefactor!”

hunks.sol: Cheongpung was still at one of the stalls that hadn’t yet closed, stuffing himself with freshly steamed fish. He thrust a hand into the air and shouted.

hunks.baseline: “I’ll finish eating and come!”
hunks.sol: “I’ll finish eating and catch up!”

hunks.sol: Unlike Emei, Qingcheng, and the Tang Clan—the prestigious powers of Sichuan Province—which had established their bases on mountains or in remote areas, the Zhuge Clan occupied the heart of a broad thoroughfare.

hunks.baseline: Just the people passing outside the carriage window numbered well over several hundred.
hunks.sol: Hundreds of people passed outside the carriage window.

hunks.sol: Their faces were deeply tanned, and whenever they spotted the carriage bearing the Zhuge Clan’s emblem, they bowed their heads.

hunks.baseline: Zhuge Gyun, sitting across from me, answered my mutter.
hunks.sol: Zhuge Gyun, who sat across from me, answered my mutter.

hunks.sol: “The Yangtze is Hubei’s lifeline. It makes the vast surrounding lands fertile, so people naturally gather here. And since every year brings a plentiful harvest, smiles never leave their faces.”

hunks.baseline: Zhuge Gyun closed his mouth, his expression suddenly serious in a way that didn’t suit him, and looked away.
hunks.sol: Zhuge Gyun fell silent and looked away, wearing a grave expression that didn’t suit him.

hunks.baseline: Something must have happened. At the Star-Array Grand Banquet, he had been an endless fountain of nonsense, so it was telling that he looked like this now.
hunks.sol: Something must have happened. At the Star-Array Grand Banquet, he had been an endless fountain of nonsense, so it was telling that even he looked like this now.

hunks.baseline: Given the mood, I didn’t ask any further questions and turned my head toward the window.
hunks.sol: Given the mood, I didn’t press him and turned toward the window.

hunks.baseline: And the more time passed, the stronger that feeling became.
hunks.sol: And the more time passed, the more that suspicion deepened.

hunks.sol: *They’re going this far in what’s practically their own front yard?*

hunks.sol: I sighed inwardly and turned my gaze beyond the carriage’s latticed window.

hunks.baseline: [^1]: This refers to a Korean Buddhist anecdote in which a monk drinks water from a skull in the dark and finds it sweet, only to recoil after seeing the skull in daylight. The phrase is used for the way perception changes once one understands the truth.
hunks.sol: [^1]: Taekyung is humorously mangling a famous Korean Buddhist anecdote about the monk Wonhyo drinking water from a skull in the dark, mistakenly attributing it to Bodhidharma.

hunks.baseline: [^2]: A *hopae* was a personal identification tablet used in premodern Korea and China.
hunks.sol: [^2]: A *hopae* was a personal identification tablet carried in premodern East Asia.
